question: Which of the following statements is correct for uniform motion?

options.text: The slope of the distance–time graph is zero.
The slope of the distance–time graph is decreasing.
The slope of the distance–time graph is constant.
The slope of the distance–time graph is increasing.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The slope of the distance–time graph is constant.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Uniform motion** refers to the motion of a body where it covers equal distances in equal intervals of time. This indicates that the speed of the object remains constant throughout the motion.
 
• The **distance–time graph** for uniform motion is a straight line that slopes upwards, indicating a constant rate of change in distance over time.
 
• The **slope of the distance–time graph** represents the speed of the object. For uniform motion, this slope remains constant, as the speed is unchanging.
 
• A **constant slope** implies there is no acceleration or deceleration, which is a characteristic feature of uniform motion.
